stories.title: Load policy definitions from a folder or a single file
stories.what: A person adds a set of policy definition files, or one file, to the working set of loaded definitions, or clears that set.
stories.why: Every other view needs loaded definitions; people must be able to start fresh or build up from several sources and learn which files were refused.

terms.name: Workspace
terms.means: The set of policy definitions currently loaded; it is not the saved policy settings.

terms.name: Definitions folder
terms.means: The folder of template files remembered for the next start; it is not a single added file.

journey.name: Load policy definitions
steps: Choose to open a folder of definitions or a single template file
Choose whether to clear the workspace first (folder only)
See any problems found while loading

criteria.says: Given a folder of definitions is chosen with "clear workspace" chosen, when it loads, then the workspace is emptied first and only that folder's definitions are shown; given it is not chosen, then they are added to the workspace and problems are reported without stopping the load.

Given a folder load fails, when the person is told "The folder could not be fully added to the workspace." with the reason, then the workspace may already be emptied or partly filled, the remembered folder is unchanged and the view is rebuilt anyway.

Given a folder was loaded, when "clear workspace" was chosen and the load did not fail, then it is remembered as the definitions folder for the next start; when the workspace was added to, the remembered folder is unchanged.

Given a single ADMX file is picked (ADMX files only), when it loads, then it is added to the workspace without emptying it and is not remembered; if it fails the person sees "The ADMX file could not be added to the workspace." with the reason.
Given a template file is loaded alone, when it is accepted, then it is added to the policies already loaded and the structures are built; when it is refused, one failure is reported.
Given definitions are loaded, when the person closes the workspace, then it empties at once with no confirmation and the view is rebuilt.

open: The legacy program picks folders and files from the person's disk and remembers a definitions folder; with upload through the service, what is remembered for the next start?

stories.title: Browse categories and policies and read their descriptions
stories.what: A person selects a category in the tree, sees its subcategories and policies in the list, highlights an item to read its description, and opens it by double-click or Enter.
stories.why: This is the main way to find a policy among thousands.

terms.name: Current category
terms.means: The category whose contents fill the list; it is not the highlighted row.

terms.name: Selected policy
terms.means: The policy last highlighted in the list; it is not the policy being edited.

journey.name: Browse policies
steps: Pick a category in the tree
Scan its subcategories and policies in the list
Highlight an item to read its description
Open a category or a policy

criteria.says: Given a category in the tree, when the person selects it, then it becomes the current category, any selected policy is cleared, and its subcategories, policies and description are shown.

Given the policy list, when the person highlights a policy, then it becomes the selected policy and any highlighted category is cleared; highlighting a category does the reverse and highlighting nothing clears both; the description follows the highlight.

Given the policy list, when the person double-clicks or presses Enter, then with no selection nothing happens, a category opens as the current category, and a policy opens its editor for the area currently shown.

Given the window or panes are resized, when the policy name column and the description pane resize, then the name column fills the list and the description labels fit the pane width with no horizontal scroll bar.

stories.title: Choose which categories and areas the list shows
stories.what: A person switches empty categories on or off and chooses to see user policies, computer policies or both.
stories.why: People work on one area at a time and need to hide clutter.

terms.name: Area
terms.means: The section a policy applies to, user or computer; it is not a category.

criteria.says: Given the "Empty Categories" menu, when the person switches it, then empty categories are shown or hidden and the view moves to the nearest visible category.
Given the area choice, when the person picks "User", then user policies show; "Computer" shows computer policies; any other choice shows both.

stories.title: Merge identical user and computer policy pairs
stories.what: A person merges policy pairs that are the same for users and computers into single policies applying to both.
stories.why: Templates often define the same setting twice; one entry per setting is easier to browse.

terms.name: Deduplication
terms.means: Merging identical user and computer policy pairs into one; it is not deleting policies.

criteria.says: Given two policies alone in the same category under the same name, one for users and one for computers, with the same explanation text and registry key, when deduplicating, then the first is removed and the second applies to both sections.
Given the person chooses to deduplicate, when it finishes, then they are told "Deduplicated N policies." with the number merged.

stories.title: Open the lists of loaded files, support rules and products
stories.what: A person opens the list of loaded template files, of all support rules, or of all products.
stories.why: People need to see what is loaded to understand what policies they can browse.

criteria.says: Given loaded definitions, when the person chooses the loaded files list, then the template files in the workspace are listed.
Given loaded definitions, when the person chooses all support rules, then every support rule is listed.
Given loaded definitions, when the person chooses all products, then the top-level products are listed ordered by name, each with its number of children.

stories.title: Use the right-click menu on categories and policies
stories.what: A person right-clicks a category or policy and picks an action that applies to it.
stories.why: The menu gives quick access to opening, editing, details and inspection.

criteria.says: Given a right-click, when the menu opens, then it shows only actions that fit: policy-only actions are hidden for a category and category-only actions for a policy.

Given the menu opens from the category tree it applies to the selected category; from elsewhere with a policy-list row selected it applies to that row; from elsewhere with no row selected it is not shown.
Given a category in the tree is right-clicked, when the menu opens, then it becomes the selected category; a left-click is left as is.
Given the menu is open, when the person chooses an item, then the category, edit window, details window or inspection window opens for the chosen object.

open: The legacy program fails with an error when the menu opens from the category tree with no selected category; what should the person see instead?

stories.title: Open a loaded template file's details from the file list
stories.what: A person opens the details of a template file from the list of loaded files, by double-click or Enter, and sees only what that file defined.
stories.why: It shows which policies, categories, products and support rules each file contributes.

terms.name: Template file
terms.means: An ADMX file of policy definitions; not the language file with its texts.

criteria.says: Given the loaded files list, when the person double-clicks a row, then that file's details open without checking a row is selected; pressing Enter checks first.
Given a template file's details, when they open, then only policies, categories (with sub-categories), products (with versions) and support rules defined in that file are listed.
Given the window changes size, when it resizes, then the namespace column fills the width left over.

open: Double-clicking with no row selected is unchecked in the legacy program; should it do nothing, like Enter?

stories.title: Browse products by version and open product details
stories.what: A person picks a product, then a major version, then sees the minor versions, and opens product details.
stories.why: Products form a three-level tree and people filter policies by them.

terms.name: Major version
terms.means: A first-level revision of a product; not a minor version.

terms.name: Minor version
terms.means: A revision beneath a major version.

criteria.says: Given a top-level product is selected, when the major versions list fills, then it shows its children ordered by version, with the heading naming the product; with none selected it is empty and prompts the person to select one.
Given a major version is selected, when the minor versions list fills, then it shows its children ordered by version, with the heading naming it; with none selected it is empty and prompts for one.
Given a list of products, when the person double-clicks or presses Enter, then product details open; with no product selected nothing happens.

stories.title: Filter the support rules list and open support rule details
stories.what: A person types text to narrow the support rules and opens the details of one, by double-click or Enter.
stories.why: There are many support rules and people look one up by name.

terms.name: Support rule
terms.means: A named condition listing the products a policy runs on; not a policy.

criteria.says: Given the support rules list, when the person double-clicks a row, then its details open without checking a row is selected; Enter checks first.

Given typed filter text, when the list updates, then only names containing it, ignoring case, show; an empty filter shows all; entries are ordered by name ignoring leading spaces and shown without them.

open: Double-clicking with no row selected is unchecked in the legacy program; should it do nothing, like Enter?

stories.title: Open details of a policy, category, product or support rule
stories.what: From a template file's details window, a person opens the details of a policy, category, product or support rule by double-click, and reads how policies relate to categories, support rules and areas.
stories.why: It explains where each item sits, including when its category or support rule is unknown.

terms.name: Orphaned
terms.means: Naming a parent or category that is not loaded; not the same as having none.

criteria.says: Given a policy in a category that exists, when its details open, then the category name shows and the category button is enabled; an unknown category shows "<orphaned from " plus the code, none shows "<uncategorized>", and the button is disabled.

Given a policy naming a support rule that exists, when its details open, then its name shows and the support button is enabled; if missing it reads "<missing: " plus the code, with no code blank, and the button is disabled.
Given a policy, when its details open, then it names the section: "User or computer", "Computer" or "User".

Given a category, when its details open, then the parent name shows and the button is enabled; a missing named parent shows "<orphaned from <parent>>" and disables it; a top-level category shows nothing.
Given a list of policies, categories, products or support rules in file details, when a row is double-clicked, then the matching details window opens.

stories.title: Move from a category to its parent category
stories.what: A person opens a category's parent from the category details window.
stories.why: It lets people walk up the category tree.

criteria.says: Given a category's details with a parent, when the person presses the parent button, then the parent's details show in the same window.

stories.title: Open category and support rule details from policy details
stories.what: A person opens the details of a policy's support rule or category from the policy details window.
stories.why: They can see where a policy applies and what it needs.

criteria.says: Given a policy's details, when the person presses the support button, then the support rule's details open.
Given a policy's details, when the person presses the category button, then the category's details open.

stories.title: Walk a product's versions and parent in product details
stories.what: A person opens a child revision or the parent product in the product details window.
stories.why: It lets people move through a product's versions.

criteria.says: Given product details with child revisions, when a child is double-clicked, then it shows in the same window; with nothing selected nothing happens.
Given product details with a parent, when the person presses the parent button, then the parent shows in the same window.
Given the window resizes, when the list changes size, then the Name column fills the list beside Version.

stories.title: Open products and nested rules from support rule details
stories.what: A person opens a product or a nested support rule from the entries in support rule details.
stories.why: It lets people follow which products a rule matches.

criteria.says: Given support rule entries, when one is double-clicked, then a product entry opens product details and a nested support rule shows in the same window; a missing product or no selection does nothing.
Given the window resizes, when the list changes size, then the Name column fills the list beside the version columns.

stories.title: Inspect a policy's definition and its semantic policy text
stories.what: A person inspects a policy's registry value, client extension, presentation and elements, copies a line, and opens the policy details. The person also reads the policy, with its comment and option values, as semantic policy text.
stories.why: Administrators need to see how a template defines a policy.

terms.name: Inspector
terms.means: The window listing a policy's definition as written in the template; not the editor of its settings.

terms.name: Semantic policy text
terms.means: A text script describing a policy's state and options; not a registry file.

criteria.says: Given the inspector, when the person presses Ctrl+C, then the selected line is copied only if a line is selected.
Given a policy, when inspected, then a "Registry value" line shows only if it names a registry value and a "Client extension" line only if it names one.
Given choice elements, when inspected, then display names resolve through the file defining the policy and choices are numbered from zero in file order.
Given a list element, when inspected, then it states "User provides value names", a prefix, or "No prefix (values named for their data)".

Given affected registry settings with no on or off setting, when inspected, then it reads "Left implicit" if the policy names a registry value, "Left to elements" if not; inside a Yes/No element always "Left implicit".
Given a policy with a presentation and elements, when inspected, then presentation details list, each item with an ID matched to the element with that ID; items without an ID show none.
Given the inspector, when the person presses the details button, then the policy details open.

Given a policy, when shown, then there is one section per area it applies to, the machine section from the computer source and comments, the user section from the user source; an uncovered area is left out.
Given a section, when shown, then the comment is included only when one is stored, and option values only when the policy is Enabled.
Given a policy line, when written, then it starts with 'C' for a machine policy or 'U' for a user policy followed by the identifier.

Given values, when written, then whole numbers have a leading #, unsigned numbers are digits, yes/no is True or False, text is single-quoted, an empty list is 'None', text lists are bracketed with double-quoted items, tables bracketed with name: value lines.
Given a comment, when written, then backslashes are doubled and each CR+LF pair is written as '\n'.

open: The legacy inspector stops with an unhandled error when a presentation item's ID matches no element; what should the person see instead?
Text holding a quote or line break, and lone line feeds in comments, cannot be read back in the legacy program; should the new version escape them or keep this?
